verses.text: “Judah’s sin is written with an iron pen tipped with diamond. It’s carved into the tablet of their hearts and into the horns of your altars.
Even their children remember their altars and Asherah poles by the leafy trees up on the high hills.
My mountain out in the open, I’m handing over your wealth, all your treasures, and your worship sites for people to loot, because of the sin all across your land.
You’ll lose the inheritance I gave you through your own doing. I’ll make you serve your enemies in a land you’ve never known. You’ve set my anger on fire, and it’ll burn forever.”
The LORD says, “A curse is on anyone who puts their trust in people, leans on human strength, and turns their heart away from the LORD.
They’ll be like a scrub bush in the desert and won’t see good when it comes. They’ll live in the driest stretches of the wilderness, on salty ground where nobody lives.
“Blessed is the person who trusts the LORD and puts their confidence in him.

They’ll be like a tree planted by the water, sending its roots out along the river. It doesn’t panic when the heat hits. Its leaves stay green. Even in a year of drought it doesn’t worry, and it keeps bearing fruit.
The heart is sneakier than anything and rotten deep down. Who can really know it?
“I’m the LORD. I search the mind and test the heart. I give each person what fits the way they’ve lived and the fruit of what they’ve done.”
A person who gets rich by cheating is like a partridge sitting on eggs it didn’t lay. Halfway through life those riches will leave them, and by the end they’ll look like a fool.
Our sanctuary is the place of a glorious throne, set high from the start.
LORD, you’re Israel’s hope. Everyone who walks away from you will end up ashamed. Those who turn away from me will be written in the dirt, because they’ve left the LORD, the spring of living water.
Heal me, LORD, and I’ll really be healed. Save me, and I’ll be saved. You’re the one I praise.
Look what they keep asking me: “Where’s the LORD’s word? Let’s see it happen right now.”
I haven’t rushed to quit being a shepherd who follows you. I didn’t wish for the day of disaster. You know that. You heard every word that came out of my mouth.
Don’t become a terror to me. You’re my shelter when disaster comes.
Let the people chasing me end up ashamed. Keep me from that shame. Let them shake with fear. Keep me from that fear. Bring the day of disaster down on them and hit them with twice the destruction.
The LORD told me, “Go stand at the People’s Gate, where the kings of Judah come in and go out, and at all the other gates of Jerusalem.
Tell them, ‘Kings of Judah, all you people of Judah and Jerusalem coming in through these gates, listen to the LORD.
The LORD says, “Watch yourselves. Don’t carry a load on the Sabbath or bring one in through Jerusalem’s gates.
Don’t carry loads out of your houses on the Sabbath, and don’t do any work. Keep the Sabbath holy, just as I told your ancestors.
But they wouldn’t listen. They wouldn’t even turn an ear my way. They stiffened their necks so they wouldn’t hear or take correction.
If you really listen to me,” says the LORD, “and bring no load through these city gates on the Sabbath but keep the day holy and do no work on it,

then kings and princes sitting on David’s throne will come through these gates. They’ll ride in chariots and on horses, with their officials and the people of Judah and Jerusalem. And this city will last forever.

People will come from Judah’s towns, the places around Jerusalem, the land of Benjamin, the lowlands, the hill country, and the South. They’ll bring burnt offerings, sacrifices, grain offerings, frankincense, and offerings of thanks to the LORD’s house.

But if you won’t listen to me and keep the Sabbath holy by leaving your loads out of the gates of Jerusalem that day, then I’ll light a fire at those gates. It’ll burn up Jerusalem’s palaces, and nobody will put it out.”’”
